messages:
AcmeApp (customer): Hey team — since ~09:10 UTC we started getting 429s on the dedicated endpoint. Traffic pattern: short bursts from CI workers, spikes for ~30s every minute. This is impacting ingestion jobs. 429 body:

```json
{\n  \"error\": \"rate_limit_exceeded\",\n  \"message\": \"throughput cap hit\",\n  \"retry_after\": 3\n}
```

We get headers: `x-rate-limit-type: throughput`, `x-reserved-pool-id: rp-42`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 168s`. Can you confirm if reserved pool throttling is in play?

Priya (support): Thanks for the report — sorry about the hit. Can you paste the full curl you used or SDK snippet and the approximate token/sec rate when the bursts happen? Also your Dedicated instance id and reserved-pool id if you have it. I'll triage. :pray:

AcmeApp (customer): Here's a minimal repro curl (redacted keys):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'X-Project-ID: acme-app' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"...","max_tokens":256}'
```

Spikes are ~4k tokens/sec sustained for 30s. Dedicated id: ded-prod-7, reserved pool reported in header rp-42.

Ethan (infra): Got it. That header `x-reserved-pool-id` means request matched a reserved capacity pool. Throttling looks like the pool hit its throughput cap. Can you confirm the SLA plan (burst allowed?) and the reserved pool config? I'll pull metrics.

Kara (dedicated-ops): Looping in dedicated ops. @Priya do we have the cap numbers for rp-42? Also sending a quick query to metrics.

Priya (support): rp-42 is on the Dedicated Business plan per our contract. I don't have the cap handy. @billing-bot can you confirm whether acme-app has burst credits or a burst policy attached?

billing-bot: Acme-app (acct 9921) — Reserved pool rp-42: committed throughput 3000 tokens/sec, burst allowance: 20% for up to 60s, billing tier: Dedicated Business (monthly commit). No recorded one-off burst purchases.

Ethan (infra): Metrics snapshot (09:08–09:12 UTC):

```
- sustained baseline: 2.8k t/s
- observed short spikes: 4.1k t/s for ~25–40s
- pool cap: 3.0k t/s
- token backlog and queueing increased, 429s aligned with spikes
```

So this is exactly throughput-cap throttling. The `x-rate-limit-reset` is a window until tokens fall under cap.

AcmeApp (customer): Is there a quick mitigation? We can't redesign burst pattern overnight. Can we smooth at the platform side or have a temporary bump?

Kara (dedicated-ops): Two options:
1) Temporary uplift of reserved pool cap from 3000 -> 6000 t/s (requires ops change and approval; can be done for short window).
2) Enable burst buffer routing: route excess to a lower-tier compatible model variant (costlier but prevents 429). We can enable automated fallback for this customer if they accept lower cost/latency.

Short-term I can apply (1) for the next 6 hours if you confirm.

Priya (support): Workaround you can apply on your side: add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s and cap concurrent requests per client to avoid synchronized spikes. SDK team has a helper `retryWithJitter()` — want the snippet? :mag_right:

AcmeApp (customer): We prefer the platform change for now. Please do (1). Also please send any logs we can use for audit.

Kara (dedicated-ops): On it. I'll request uplift and post when done. ETA ~8min. I'll also mark a postmortem item to discuss changing default burst allowance for Business pools.

deploy-bot: Change request cr-879 opened by Kara, scope: reserved-pool uplift rp-42 -> 6000 t/s for 6h. Approvals: auto-approved for emergency ops.

Ethan (infra): Applying change to serving layer now — updating routing table so that pool capacity = 6000. Pushing config in 2 phases to avoid flapping.

Kara (dedicated-ops): Done — rp-42 cap updated to 6000 t/s at 09:22 UTC. Observing metrics now.

Ethan (infra): Metrics post-change (09:22–09:26 UTC):

```
- observed spikes: 4.2k t/s handled, no 429s
- avg latency during spikes: +28ms p50, p95 +80ms (expected due to higher utilization)
- queue depth returned to normal
```

AcmeApp (customer): Confirmed — 429s stopped. Thanks all!

Priya (support): Great. Action items:
- Kara: temporary uplift for 6h completed (rp-42 -> 6000 t/s). Please confirm when you revert or if customer requests extension.
- Ethan: file infra ticket to add an alert when pool usage > 90% for 3 consecutive minutes (so we catch recurring cases).
- Priya: update runbook for Dedicated to include: check `x-reserved-pool-id`, confirm pool cap against billing, consider enabling fallback routing as default for Business?
- Billing: consider offering burst add-on for predictable bursts.

Kara (dedicated-ops): I'll revert at 15:22 UTC unless Acme asks to extend. Also adding postmortem note to dedicated ops board.

billing-bot: Noted — creating a follow-up invoice quote for burst addon.

AcmeApp (customer): Appreciate the fast turnaround. Could you also share the exact header we can check in our logs to auto-alert before we hit cap?

Ethan (infra): Watch for `x-reserved-pool-utilization` in response headers (0.0–1.0). We'll add it to responses for the next rolling deploy. For now, use `x-rate-limit-reset` and the `x-reserved-pool-id` to correlate.

Priya (support): Closing thread once Kara reverts or we confirm a longer-term plan. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
